Claude Code Contrast Setup

Step-through instructions for raising the contrast between your messages and Claude's in a Ghostty terminal. Verified against Claude Code 2.1.229 and Ghostty 1.3.1 on macOS. Every color below is measured, not eyeballed.

The problem, measured

In viewMode: "focus", Claude Code draws a background block behind your messages using the theme token userMessageBackground. In dark-daltonized that token is rgb(55,55,55) (#373737). Ghostty's default background is #282c34.

TokenValueContrast vs #282c34
userMessageBackground#3737371.18:1
subtle#5050501.74:1
inactive#9999994.91:1
briefLabelYou#7ab4e86.35:1
briefLabelClaude#d777574.44:1

This is a luminance failure, not a hue failure. That is why switching to the colorblind-friendly theme did not help. Every token the daltonized theme changes is a hue substitution. The one cue that separates your text from Claude's is a brightness block, and at 1.18:1 it is invisible to everyone, colorblind or not. Fixing it means raising luminance separation and adding a second, redundant cue that does not depend on hue at all.

What you are about to change

  1. Darken the Ghostty background so a dark block can still separate from it.
  2. Create a Claude Code custom theme that overrides five tokens.
  3. Activate it and re-measure.

Two independent cues result: a clearly filled slate blue bar behind your messages at 4.42:1, up from 1.18:1, and a strong blue-versus-amber pair on the You and Claude labels. The label pair is the one to trust long term, because it survives all three types of dichromacy (numbers in the reference section). The block is deliberately pushed to the top of its usable range, and step 2 explains the ceiling that stops it going further.

Total time: about 15 minutes, including verification.

Step 0. Back out point

Snapshot what you have now

2 minutes

Both files you are about to touch are tiny. Copy them first so rollback is one command.

mkdir -p ~/Developer/claude-code-contrast/backup
cp ~/.claude/settings.json ~/Developer/claude-code-contrast/backup/settings.json.bak
cp "$HOME/Library/Application Support/com.mitchellh.ghostty/config.ghostty" \
   ~/Developer/claude-code-contrast/backup/config.ghostty.bak
ls -la ~/Developer/claude-code-contrast/backup

Step 1. Darken the Ghostty background

Write the Ghostty config

3 minutes

Ghostty on macOS reads ~/Library/Application Support/com.mitchellh.ghostty/config.ghostty. Yours is empty, so nothing is being overwritten.

cat >> "$HOME/Library/Application Support/com.mitchellh.ghostty/config.ghostty" <<'EOF'

# Contrast baseline for Claude Code. See ~/Developer/claude-code-contrast/
background = #000000
foreground = #e8eaed
minimum-contrast = 2
bold-is-bright = true
EOF

What each line does:

SettingEffect
background = #000000Pure black. Drops background luminance from 0.0250 to 0.0000, which is the maximum headroom available for the block in step 2. Every point of separation the block gets is bought here.
foreground = #e8eaedSlightly off-white default text. Pure white on near-black is harsh over long sessions.
minimum-contrast = 2Forces any foreground text below 2:1 against its own cell background up to 2:1. Catches dim text from other CLI tools. It does not fix background-versus-background blocks, which is why Step 2 is still required.
bold-is-bright = trueBold ANSI text uses the bright palette slot, adding a luminance cue to bold.

Keep minimum-contrast at 2. Higher values start rewriting colors you deliberately chose. At 2, none of the Step 2 label colors are touched, because they all sit above 11:1.

Reload with Cmd+Shift+, in Ghostty, then confirm the values took:

/Applications/Ghostty.app/Contents/MacOS/ghostty +show-config \
  | grep -E 'background|foreground|minimum-contrast|bold-is-bright'

Step 2. Create the Claude Code custom theme

Write the theme file

5 minutes

Claude Code reads custom themes from ~/.claude/themes/. The slug is the filename without .json. This mechanism is not in the documentation, but it is fully wired: the file is parsed, each override value is validated, and only keys that already exist in the base theme are applied. An unrecognized key is silently ignored rather than causing an error, so a typo fails quietly. Check your spelling against the reference table at the bottom.

mkdir -p ~/.claude/themes
cat > ~/.claude/themes/high-contrast-cb.json <<'EOF'
{
  "name": "High contrast (colorblind)",
  "base": "dark-daltonized",
  "overrides": {
    "userMessageBackground": "#5a7596",
    "userMessageBackgroundHover": "#6c8aa8",
    "composerSidebarBackground": "#2b3a4a",
    "briefLabelYou": "#8ecbff",
    "briefLabelClaude": "#ffc14d",
    "subtle": "#7d8590",
    "inactive": "#b0b8c2"
  }
}
EOF
python3 -c "import json;print('valid JSON:', bool(json.load(open('$HOME/.claude/themes/high-contrast-cb.json'))))"

Why each value:

TokenWasNowResult
userMessageBackground#373737#5a75961.18:1 to 4.42:1
userMessageBackgroundHover#464646#6c8aa85.84:1
composerSidebarBackground#262626#2b3a4a1.81:1
briefLabelYou#7ab4e8#8ecbff12.14:1
briefLabelClaude#d77757#ffc14d12.99:1
subtle#505050#7d85901.74:1 to 5.63:1
inactive#999999#b0b8c24.91:1 to 10.48:1

The block is a distinctly lighter slate blue now, not a subtle tint. At 4.42:1 it reads as a filled bar rather than a shading, which is the point. It also shares a hue family with the blue You label, so the two cues reinforce each other instead of competing. Claude keeps the warm amber. Blue against amber is the strongest axis available across all three dichromacies.

The ceiling, and why the block stops at #5a7596. The text inside the block is drawn with the global text token. The renderer paints text over userMessageBackground, and there is no separate token for the block's foreground. So every point of contrast the block gains against the terminal background is a point your own typed text loses against the block, at close to a one-for-one exchange. #5a7596 is the brightest value where both numbers still clear 4.5:1 (block 4.42:1, your text on it 4.75:1). Step 5 has the ladder if you want to push past it, along with what it costs.

One thing to look at once this is live: the You and Claude labels measure 2.75:1 and 2.94:1 against the brighter block, versus 12:1 against the terminal background. If those labels render inside the block rather than beside it, they will look worse than they did before, and the right move is to step the block back down to #4f6b8e and keep the labels crisp. Check this in step 4 before you commit to the value.

Step 3. Activate it

Point the theme setting at the custom slug

2 minutes

A custom theme is referenced as custom: plus the slug. Your settings.json currently reads "theme": "dark-daltonized".

Correction, checked on this machine. ~/.claude/settings.json is not a symlink into gutils, despite what the gutils CLAUDE.md says. It is a regular file, and it has drifted from claude-code/settings.json in six places, including the theme, the superpowers plugin flag, and viewMode. ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and ~/.claude/hooks are still symlinked as documented, so settings.json is the lone exception.

Two consequences. Your theme change stays local to this machine rather than syncing. And running claude-code/setup.sh could overwrite the live file with the gutils copy, which would revert the theme and lose focus mode. Reconcile the two before you next run setup, by copying live over the gutils copy and then re-linking.

python3 - <<'EOF'
import json, pathlib
p = pathlib.Path.home() / '.claude' / 'settings.json'
d = json.loads(p.read_text())
print('was:', d.get('theme'))
d['theme'] = 'custom:high-contrast-cb'
p.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=2) + '\n')
print('now:', d['theme'])
EOF

Then restart Claude Code. Themes are cached at startup, so an open session will not pick up a brand new file. Confirm with /theme: your theme should be listed and selected.

The interactive route works too if you would rather click than edit files: /theme, then Ctrl+E opens the custom theme editor with a live preview. The set of tokens that editor exposes is not confirmed, though, and it may not surface all seven. The file above is the deterministic path.

Step 4. Verify

Look, then measure

3 minutes

The eye test first. In a live session, scroll back over a few turns and check three things:

Then the measurement. verify.py already sits next to this file, so just run python3 ~/Developer/claude-code-contrast/verify.py. It reads your actual theme file, so it also catches typos in the override keys, which Claude Code otherwise discards without complaint. The listing below is the same logic, for reference.

import json, pathlib

BG = '#000000'  # your Ghostty background

def srgb(h):
    h = h.lstrip('#')
    return [int(h[i:i+2], 16) / 255 for i in (0, 2, 4)]

def lin(c):
    return [(v / 12.92 if v <= 0.04045 else ((v + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4) for v in c]

def lum(h):
    r, g, b = lin(srgb(h))
    return 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b

def cr(a, b):
    la, lb = lum(a), lum(b)
    hi, lo = max(la, lb), min(la, lb)
    return (hi + 0.05) / (lo + 0.05)

TARGETS = {
    'userMessageBackground': 4.0,
    'briefLabelYou': 7.0,
    'briefLabelClaude': 7.0,
    'subtle': 4.5,
    'inactive': 7.0,
}

path = pathlib.Path.home() / '.claude' / 'themes' / 'high-contrast-cb.json'
overrides = json.loads(path.read_text())['overrides']

fail = 0
for token, floor in TARGETS.items():
    value = overrides.get(token)
    if value is None:
        print(f'MISSING  {token}')
        fail += 1
        continue
    ratio = cr(value, BG)
    ok = ratio >= floor
    fail += 0 if ok else 1
    print(f'{"PASS" if ok else "FAIL"}  {token:26s} {value}  {ratio:5.2f}:1  (floor {floor})')

print('\nall targets met' if not fail else f'\n{fail} problem(s)')

Step 5. If it is still not enough

One dial, in one direction

2 minutes per attempt

Change userMessageBackground only, and move one row at a time. Every row is measured against a pure black terminal background. The two columns move in opposite directions and their product is close to constant, which is the whole shape of the problem: there is no value that maximizes both.

ValueBlock vs backgroundYour text on blockVerdict
#3737371.76:111.90:1Stock. Block invisible.
#4f6b8e3.83:15.49:1Back off to here if the block feels loud
#5a75964.42:14.75:1Recommended. Last row where both clear 4.5:1
#63809f5.12:14.10:1Your text below AA
#6c8aa85.84:13.60:1Your text noticeably washed out
#7593b16.56:13.20:1Do not

#5a7596 is already 3.8 times the separation the stock theme gave you. If that still is not enough, the honest answer is that the block alone cannot get you there, because the block and your own text are fighting over the same luminance budget. At that point the fix is a cue that is not a background at all, which is what the upstream issue asks for. In the meantime, lean harder on the label pair and on viewMode: "verbose", which adds structural separation between turns rather than color.

Two other levers, if the block approach is not working for you at all:

  • viewMode accepts default, verbose, or focus. You are on focus, which is what produces the You and Claude labels in the first place. verbose adds more structural chrome between turns, which is a cue that does not rely on color at all.
  • theme: "dark-ansi" hands every color to Ghostty's 16-color palette, so one Ghostty theme governs Claude Code and every other tool in your terminal. Ghostty ships 463 themes, browse them with ghostty +list-themes. The cost is losing the per-token control you just set up, since userMessageBackground becomes ansi:blackBright.

Before and after

Upstream

Filed as anthropics/claude-code#86221. The full text is on GitHub, but the argument is captured here so this page stands alone offline.

The report leads with the 1.18:1 measurement across three common terminal backgrounds, then makes the case that this is a bug rather than a preference: diffing dark-daltonized against plain dark, the tokens userMessageBackground, userMessageBackgroundHover, subtle, inactive and text are byte-identical. Every token the daltonized theme changes is a hue substitution, so the theme sold as colorblind-friendly leaves untouched the one cue carrying no hue information.

It asks for three things in preference order. First, a channel that is not color at all, a left rule or a gutter glyph, because that is the only fix without a ceiling. Second, raising the dark-theme value to around #5a7596. Third, decoupling the block's foreground from the global text token, since that coupling is what creates the ceiling. It cross-references #77041 (the token is shared with the conversation selector and the Plugin/Skill/MCP badges), #77129, and #83570.

A follow-up comment corrects one thing in the original report. It implied the You and Claude labels remain as a fallback when the block is invisible. They do not. The brief layout that draws them is gated behind CLAUDE_CODE_BRIEF or the off-by-default tengu_kairos_brief flag, and the block and labels are mutually exclusive by construction (Dqn = Pqn ? void 0 : "userMessageBackground"). So in a default install the 1.18:1 block is the only separator and there is no fallback at all, which makes the bug slightly worse than first described. The comment also notes an asymmetry: the assistant-side label checks isBriefOnly alone while the user-side label and the block suppression check isBriefOnly and the gate, so a configuration exists where Claude renders but You does not.

Notes for the write-up

Everything needed to draft offline, so nothing has to be re-derived.

  1. The hook. The theme labeled colorblind-friendly shipped a cue at 1.18:1. Not a bad color choice, an absent one. And it is identical to the non-colorblind theme in exactly the tokens that matter.
  2. The reframe. Colorblind-safe palettes substitute hues. This cue never carried hue in the first place, it carried brightness. Daltonizing a luminance cue is a no-op. That is the generalizable lesson and it applies well beyond this one tool.
  3. The constraint that makes it interesting. You cannot just brighten the block. Its foreground is the global text token, so block visibility and the legibility of your own typing draw on one shared luminance budget. Their product is roughly constant. There is no free win, only a chosen point on a curve, and #5a7596 is where both sides still clear 4.5:1.
  4. The method beat. Every number here is computed, not eyeballed. Worth noting that Claude Code's own binary contains the string "❌ Eyeballing colorblind-safety. \"These look different enough.\"", which is a good joke on the situation and a fair standard to be held to.
  5. The payoff. Validating the label pair against a grid search: blue and amber scores 54.2 worst-case across all three dichromacies versus 59.7 for the best alternative, but 96.2 and 107.5 on protanopia and deuteranopia versus 59.7 and 72.6. Those two are about 8% of males, tritanopia about 0.01%. Optimize the common case, accept the rare one. Show the work rather than asserting the choice.

Numbers worth quoting exactly: 1.18:1 stock on Ghostty default, 1.38:1 on VS Code dark+, 1.76:1 on pure black, 3:1 WCAG floor for non-text UI, 4.42:1 after, 3.8x improvement, 4.75:1 for your own text on the block, 11.90:1 for text on the stock block (the detail that proves the block, not the text, was broken).

Angles deliberately not taken, in case they are better for your audience: the undocumented ~/.claude/themes/ mechanism as its own post; the silent-discard-on-typo behavior as a lesson in configuration design; the shared-token problem in #77041 as a theming architecture piece.

Rollback

cp ~/Developer/claude-code-contrast/backup/settings.json.bak ~/.claude/settings.json
cp ~/Developer/claude-code-contrast/backup/config.ghostty.bak \
   "$HOME/Library/Application Support/com.mitchellh.ghostty/config.ghostty"
rm ~/.claude/themes/high-contrast-cb.json

Restart Claude Code and reload Ghostty with Cmd+Shift+, to return to where you started. All three targets are plain files on this machine, so these copies are the whole undo. There is also backup/high-contrast-cb.json.pre-bump.bak, which is the theme as it stood before the block was bumped, if you want the gentler values back rather than nothing.

Reference

Colorblind safety of the label pair

Perceptual distance between You at #8ecbff and Claude at #ffc14d, simulated with the Viénot dichromat model and measured as CIELAB delta E. Anything above roughly 25 is comfortably distinguishable.

VisionYou renders asClaude renders asDelta E
Normal#8ecbff#ffc14d97.8
Protanopia#c2c2ff#cdcd4c96.2
Deuteranopia#babaff#d8d846107.5
Tritanopia#81d3d3#ffb7b754.2

For comparison, the stock dark-daltonized pair (#7ab4e8 against #d77757) scores 65.3 under protanopia and 79.8 under deuteranopia. Usable, but both colors also sit lower against the background at 6.35:1 and 4.44:1, so the pair was doing less work than it could.

Theme file format

~/.claude/themes/<slug>.json

{
  "name": "<display name shown in /theme>",
  "base": "dark | light | dark-daltonized | light-daltonized | dark-ansi | light-ansi",
  "overrides": { "<token>": "<color>", ... }
}

Activate with  "theme": "custom:<slug>"  in settings.json

Accepted color formats: #rrggbb, #rgb, rgb(r,g,b), ansi256(0-255), and ansi:<name> where name is one of the sixteen standard slots such as blue or blueBright. Anything else is discarded and the base value is kept.

Tokens worth knowing

TokenWhere it shows up
userMessageBackgroundBlock behind your messages in focus mode. The main fix.
userMessageBackgroundHoverSame block, hovered.
briefLabelYou / briefLabelClaudeThe You and Claude labels in focus mode.
composerSidebarBackgroundGutter beside the input composer.
text / inverseTextPrimary body text and its inverse.
subtle / inactiveDe-emphasized text. Both were the worst offenders after the block.
bashMessageBackgroundColorBlock behind bash command output.
memoryBackgroundColorBlock behind memory notices.
diffAdded / diffRemovedDiff backgrounds. Green against red by default, worth overriding separately.
success / error / warningStatus colors.
selectionBgSelected row in pickers and menus.

There are roughly seventy tokens in total, including a *_FOR_SUBAGENTS_ONLY family that colors subagent output and a rainbow_* family. Dump the full list for your version with:

strings -a "$(readlink -f "$(which claude)")" \
  | grep -oE '\{autoAccept:[^{}]*\}' | head -1 | tr ',' '\n'

Known fragility

The custom theme mechanism is real and stable in 2.1.229, but it is undocumented, which means token names are an internal detail and can be renamed without a changelog entry. Unknown keys fail silently rather than loudly. If contrast quietly regresses after a Claude Code upgrade, re-run verify.py first, then re-dump the token list with the command above and diff the names against your overrides.

Verified against Claude Code 2.1.229 and Ghostty 1.3.1, macOS 25.5.0, 2026-08-12. Contrast ratios are WCAG 2.x relative luminance. Dichromat simulation is Viénot 1999.
